$comment: TF-C86 (D-CSUBSET-STDARG-F001A): RUN witness that the world's standard `#ifndef __has_include / #define __has_include(x) 0 / #endif` portability shim (Apple SDK sys/cdefs.h:91-93, glibc, musl) CANNOT shadow the __has_include operator DSS provides. The shim is dead code on a compiler that has the operator; DSS used to take it, replace the operator with a function-like macro answering 0, and thereby turn every `#if __has_include(...)`-guarded include into a skipped splice and then a hard `F001A: not found` on a header that was present all along (MEASURED: 5 of the 7 macho F001A on the sqlite corpus). Exit 42 = 40 (the guarded header's spliced `#define`) + 2 (the guarded header's function, codegenned and LINKED) -- only a REAL textual splice produces both, which is why this is a run witness and not a compile-only one. Format-NEUTRAL (C23 6.10.1, not a platform feature) so all three formats run it. The `#else` arm and the two definedness arms are `#error`s: a shadowed operator fails the BUILD loud rather than silently returning a different exit code. Release arm runs the optimizer over the spliced call. RED-ON-DISABLE (MEASURED): revert the `isConditionalInclusionOperator` arm in MacroExpander::isDefined -> `#ifndef __has_include` goes live -> the `#error` fires -> the build fails.
